messages:
anya: RFC follow-up: proposing a delta-patching strategy for disconnected / air-gapped installs. Goal: reduce bandwidth for large model/runtime bundles by shipping content-addressed delta chunks + signed manifest, with fallback to full images. Questions for runtime/ops: how do we do atomic apply + verification + safe rollback? RFC: https://r.rw/delta-patch-rfc (PR in draft).

samir: high level - love the bandwidth savings, but curious about complexity tradeoffs. Can we start with signed tarballs + optional rsync-style diffs? Many air-gapped customers won't have rsync endpoints.

lee: main safety note: deltas require deterministic layout and reproducible builds (or at least deterministic manifests). If we can't guarantee reproducible image bytes, the delta algorithm will explode in churn. Also how do we handle interrupted apply? We need an atomic swap.

marco: proposal sketch: 1) content-addressed chunking (fixed-size chunk + rolling hash for edges) -> Merkle manifest. 2) sign the manifest with our release key. 3) applier fetches chunks, verifies hash tree locally, applies into a staging rootfs. 4) healthcheck the staging root (start services in chroot/container) and then symlink/swap. Fallback to full-image if manifest verification fails or missing chunks. Keep metadata for rollback (previous symlink target + manifest id).

anya: that covers the main asks. A few followups: how do we store/rotate verification keys for air-gapped installs? and how do we surface progress/partial failures to customers?

samir: for key rotation, simplest: include a pinned public key in the installer and support an "offline trusted keys" directory that admins can update. We should avoid requiring the customer to fetch keys from our KMS. For telemetry/progress, the applier can emit a text log under /var/log/redwood/upgrade-<ts>.log and an artifacts index under /var/lib/redwood/upgrades/<id> with status.json.

lee: about interrupted apply: do NOT mutate live rootfs in-place. Write into /var/lib/redwood/staging/<id> and then do an atomic switch via symlink or mount namespace. Example atomic swap snippet: 

```sh
set -e
staging=/var/lib/redwood/staging/$ID
release=/opt/redwood/current
new=/var/lib/redwood/releases/$ID
# unpack into $new, run healthcheck
ln -sfn $new $release
# ensure services reference $release path
```

samir: also add a preflight checksum step before staging unpack. If chunk verify fails, try to re-fetch or fall back. ops teams prefer retry-with-backoff for flaky links (customers often transfer via USB or slow proxy).

deploy-bot: deploy: patch rollout started on node-42 at 2025-11-08T14:12:07Z :rocket:

ops-bot: node-42: chunk verification FAILED (sha256 mismatch) on chunk 00012, stored at /tmp/rdw/chunks. Marking attempt=1

lee: re: failed chunk - applier should keep a download cache and a manifest -> chunk map so we can resume. Also include chunk-level signatures optional (probably overkill), but manifest-level signature is minimum.

marco: We should design a 3-tier fallback: 1) delta streaming apply, 2) full image apply (signed), 3) manual offline recovery instructions. Keep a compact rollback manifest (previous release id, timestamp, reason). All metadata should be stored under /var/lib/redwood/upgrades/<id> and be human-readable.

anya: air-gapped key trust: include a small CA bundle and an admin CLI to inject additional trusted public keys offline (cli: `redwood trust add --pubkey /path/to/key.pub`). We should document key rotation flow in RFC.

samir: one more ops detail: avoid using ephemeral in-memory keys for verification. Use persistent truststore with file permissions and chown root:root, mode 600.

marco: implementation notes: we can reuse our existing artifact server code for chunk serving, and extend the runtime applier as a standalone binary. Keep applier idempotent and crash-safe.

anya: consensus check: proceed with prototype of content-addressed delta + Merkle manifest + signed manifest, staging apply + atomic symlink swap, chunk cache + retry, fallback to signed full image, and clear rollback metadata. Action items: 1) marco -> prototype chunking library, 2) lee -> spec for atomic swap and healthchecks, 3) samir -> ops checklist + offline key UX, 4) anya -> update RFC with these decisions and add key-rotation appendix.

samir: +1 :+1:

marco: noted. I'll open an initial PR with a chunker PoC and tests.
